title: Merge Sorted Array
statement: `nums1` has length m + n. The first m elements are a sorted array, and the last n slots are placeholders. `nums2` has n sorted elements. Merge nums2 into nums1 so that nums1 becomes one sorted array, and return it.
hints: Writing from the left overwrites values in nums1 that have not been merged yet.
The largest remaining element is at the tail of one of the two arrays.
Fill nums1 from index m + n - 1 backward.

approaches.name: Copy and sort
approaches.explanation: Place nums2 into the tail and sort.

approaches.name: Reverse two pointers
approaches.explanation: Merge from the back into free slots.

editorial: Three pointers: i at the last real element of nums1, j at the last element of nums2, and k at the last slot of nums1. Write the larger of nums1[i] and nums2[j] at k, and retreat that pointer. If nums2 is exhausted first, the remaining nums1 prefix is already in place.
reference_solution:
from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Tuple
from collections import Counter, OrderedDict, defaultdict, deque
import heapq

def merge_sorted(nums1: list[int], m: int, nums2: list[int], n: int) -> list[int]:
    i, j, k = m - 1, n - 1, m + n - 1
    while j >= 0:
        if i >= 0 and nums1[i] > nums2[j]:
            nums1[k] = nums1[i]
            i -= 1
        else:
            nums1[k] = nums2[j]
            j -= 1
        k -= 1
    return nums1
